title: Norwegian tax residence detachment (skattemessig utflytting)
description: Emigrating from Norway does not automatically end Norwegian tax residence. For a person who has been tax-resident for 10 years or more, residence ceases only after three consecutive income years in which they spend fewer than 61 days per year in Norway and neither they nor close family have a dwelling available in Norway. Shorter-term residents can break residence in the year presence drops below the day thresholds. Detachment must be actively documented to Skatteetaten; otherwise the mover stays exposed to worldwide Norwegian taxation and dual filing for up to three trailing years.

title: Deregistration from the National Population Register (Folkeregisteret)
description: A move abroad expected to last six months or more must be reported to Skatteetaten (folkeregisteret) as a move abroad (flytting til utlandet), filed digitally at skatteetaten.no or on paper before departure. This is separate from tax detachment and affects access to public services, BankID and Helfo. Not reporting can cause benefit overpayments and complicate later re-registration.

title: A1 certificate for continued Norwegian social-security coverage (posted worker)
description: If the employee stays on a Norwegian contract and is posted to France, an A1 certificate from NAV confirms Norwegian social-security legislation continues to apply and avoids double contributions. It is valid up to 24 months for postings under EEA Regulation 883/2004. The employer normally applies; without the A1, French URSSAF contributions fall due from day one.

title: French posted-worker declaration (SIPSI) filed by the employer
description: For a worker posted to France, French law requires the employer to file a prior posting declaration on the SIPSI portal and to appoint a representative in France. This is a receiving-country obligation distinct from the A1. Note: the Arbeidstilsynet notification referenced in generic checklists applies to postings INTO Norway, not out of it. Non-declaration exposes the employer to French labour-inspection penalties.
evidence_quote: Permet à un employeur établi à l'étranger de transmettre une déclaration de détachement à la Direction départementale en charge de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités (DDETS ou DDETS-PP, ex-Direccte) du lieu où doit être effectuée la prestation. Cette déclaration doit être effectuée avant le début de la prestation.

title: Social-security coordination and totalization (NO-FR)
description: Although Norway is outside the EU, it applies EEA Regulation 883/2004, so insurance periods in Norway and France are aggregated for pension and benefit purposes. The employee should obtain documentation of Norwegian insurance periods from NAV to protect future French and aggregated entitlements.

title: Loss of National Insurance (folketrygden) membership on emigration
description: Compulsory membership of the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme normally ends when a person emigrates and is no longer resident or working in Norway. Voluntary membership (frivillig medlemskap) can be applied for through NAV to preserve pension accrual and health rights, but it must be requested within deadlines and is not automatic.

title: Occupational pension (OTP / AFP) accrued rights on leaving employment
description: On ending Norwegian employment, accrued defined-contribution occupational pension (OTP) is converted to a paid-up policy (pensjonskapitalbevis) that the individual retains and can consolidate. Eligibility for AFP (avtalefestet pensjon) can be forfeited if the qualifying employment conditions are broken by the move - a commonly overlooked loss.
evidence_quote: Arbeidstaker som slutter i virksomheten, skal meldes ut av virksomhetens pensjonsordning, og vil få tilsendt et pensjonskapitalbevis fra pensjonsleverandøren.

title: Norwegian exit tax on unrealised share gains (utflyttingsskatt)
description: Norway levies an exit tax on latent gains on shares and fund units when tax residence ends, where total latent gains exceed NOK 500,000. The rules were tightened in 2024 (changes to the former lapse period and to payment arrangements). It requires valuation and filing and can be significant for an employee holding shares or options.

title: Norwegian bank account, BankID and non-resident status
description: Banks such as DNB and Nordea may restrict or reclassify accounts once a customer is registered as non-resident, and BankID is tied to a Norwegian mobile number and national-registry status. Keeping an active account and IBAN for trailing tax, pension and salary matters usually requires notifying the bank and securing a valid electronic-ID method before deregistration.

title: Trailing Norwegian tax-return (skattemelding) obligations
description: A Norwegian tax return (skattemelding) must be filed for the year of departure and for any later year in which Norwegian tax residence or Norwegian-source income persists - for example during the three-year detachment window or for retained Norwegian property. The filing obligation does not end on the day of the move.

title: Health cover: Helfo deregistration and S1 / EHIC
description: Ending folketrygden membership ends Helfo coverage and invalidates the Norwegian EHIC for continued residence abroad. If the employee stays insured in Norway while resident in France (for example under an A1), an S1 document from Helfo/NAV registers him for French healthcare at Norwegian cost. Otherwise he must enrol in French social security (PUMA / CPAM).
evidence_quote: If you are a member of the National Insurance Scheme in Norway and are a citizen either of Norway, another EU/EEA country, or Switzerland, you are entitled to a European Health Insurance Card from Norway.

title: Exporting a Norwegian-registered car to France (non-EU customs frontier)
description: Because Norway is in the EEA but NOT the EU customs union, moving a Norwegian-registered vehicle into France is an import into the EU. It can trigger a French customs declaration and, unless transfer-of-residence relief applies, French VAT and customs on the vehicle, plus re-registration (carte grise) and a quitus fiscal. This is a frequently missed cost and a genuine NO-specific quirk.
evidence_quote: Vous devez acquitter les droits de douane et la TVA, ou la TVA seule le cas échéant, auprès d'un bureau de douane, en vue de l'immatriculation de votre véhicule dans une série normale, dans les cas suivants : véhicule originaire et en provenance d'un pays non membre de la Communauté européenne

title: Removal / household goods: EU import and transfer-of-residence relief
description: Household goods shipped from Norway (non-EU) to France cross the EU customs frontier. Duty and VAT relief for personal property on transfer of normal residence (ToR / franchise de demenagement) is available but must be claimed with an inventory and proof of prior residence abroad; without the paperwork, French customs can assess import charges.

title: Norwegian driving licence validity in France
description: A Norwegian (EEA) driving licence is valid for driving in France without exchange for as long as it remains valid; exchange is only required on expiry, loss, or after certain offences. No action is strictly required on departure, but the licence should be renewed in Norway before it lapses because renewing an EEA licence from abroad is difficult.

title: Cessation of Norwegian child benefit (barnetrygd) and CAF coordination
description: Norwegian barnetrygd generally stops when the family emigrates. Family benefits are then coordinated under EEA rules; if the family becomes resident and covered in France, French family benefits (CAF) apply. NAV must be notified to avoid overpayment and clawback, and the country with primary competence must be established.

title: Trailing Norwegian tax on retained Norwegian real estate
description: If the employee keeps and rents out Norwegian property after the move, Norway retains taxing rights on that real-estate income (and on gains on eventual sale) under the NO-FR tax treaty, even after residence ends. This creates a continuing Norwegian filing obligation alongside French worldwide-income reporting, with treaty relief to prevent double taxation.
